title: Stop Making Models Bigger, Make Them Behave — Kobie Crawford, Snorkel

primary.label: Post-Training & Continual Learning
primary.rationale: Selected by Jev (System One, jev-1.13.0) from the 17-category taxonomy using the talk's summary, takeaways, concepts and technologies (confidence 99%).

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The presentation details using RL fine-tuning (GRPO) to adapt a 4B model's tool-use behavior for financial analysis, explicitly covering data generation and evaluation rubrics.

summary: Kobe Crawford, Developer Advocate at Snorkel — a 'Frontier Data Frontier AI Data Lab' — presents research conducted in partnership with UC Berkeley's RLLM (Agentic Project) lab. The central thesis challenges the enterprise practice of scaling to larger models when performance falls short. The research objective is making a 4B parameter model outperform a 235B parameter model on a tool-use task for financial analysis. Crawford frames enterprise use cases as requiring reliability, safety, security, and on-premise deployment — priorities favoring smaller models. The 'Terence Tao effect,' a term from the RLLM team, captures the idea that a financial analyst doesn't need a model brilliant at all mathematics; deeper reasoning isn't always the answer. Snorkel's intuition is that RL is better for changing behavior (like tool-use discipline) than for changing core knowledge. A key demonstration shows Qwen 3 235B responding to 'What is the year-over-year growth rate of YouTube ads revenue from 23 to 24?' The model queried a non-existent table without inspecting the environment, tried again with no result, and then hallucinated an answer — illustrating that greater reasoning did not compensate for lack of tool-use discipline. Snorkel built a self-contained FinQA environment (available on PrimeIntellect, OpenEnv, and Hugging Face spaces) with 290 samples and 79 harder multi-table FinQA reasoning samples. The RL approach uses GRPO on a 4B model, with a 21-hour job costing under $500 per run. Pass-at-one essentially doubled. The fine-tuned 4B model demonstrated disciplined tool use: it first called get_table_names, then inspected schema via get_table_info, ran a query, hit a column error, self-corrected, and got the right answer. Single-table-only training yielded the greatest uplift and transferred to harder multi-table problems, improving FinQA reasoning from 13.9% to 26.6%. Crawford emphasizes that the core failure mode was tool discipline, not reasoning depth, and advocates rubric-based evals — breaking responses into granular questions — to identify which specific behavior to fix before writing training data. GRPO still uses a single value for the RL cycle.
whyItMatters: The talk connects its engineering abstractions, implementation choices, and AI/product implications into one practical system view.

sections.title: Introduction and Snorkel Context
sections.summary: Crawford introduces himself as Developer Advocate at Snorkel, explains Snorkel's focus on data quality with experts in the loop, and previews the talk's thesis about applying the right data to the right problem rather than scaling models.

sections.title: Research Objective and Enterprise Motivation
sections.summary: The goal is making a 4B parameter model outperform a 235B model on financial analysis tool use, in partnership with UC Berkeley's RLLM lab. Enterprise use cases favor smaller models for cost, speed, security, and on-premise deployment. RL is positioned as better for changing behavior than core knowledge.

sections.title: The Terence Tao Effect
sections.summary: The RLLM team's 'Terence Tao effect' concept: using a much larger, smarter model for financial analysis tasks is overkill, like taking a sledgehammer to crack a walnut. A financial analyst doesn't need deep mathematical brilliance to run SQL queries and do arithmetic.

sections.title: Qwen 3 235B Demo Failure
sections.summary: The 235B model failed the YouTube ad revenue YoY growth question by querying a non-existent table without inspecting the environment, tried again with no result, then hallucinated an answer — demonstrating that greater reasoning did not compensate for lack of tool-use discipline.

sections.title: Data Generation and RL Approach
sections.summary: Snorkel generates high-quality data with experts in the loop (PhD-level, industry veterans), verifies tasks are queryable with verifiable answers, and applies GRPO RL starting from a 4B parameter model. The fine-tuned 4B model's response will be shown later for contrast.

sections.title: FinQA Environment and Training Cost
sections.summary: Snorkel built a self-contained FinQA environment with no external dependencies, available on PrimeIntellect, OpenEnv, and Hugging Face spaces. The RL job ran in about 21 hours costing under $500 per run, demonstrating RL can be affordable and tractable for improving smaller models.

sections.title: Results and 4B Model Tool Discipline Demo
sections.summary: The 4B model outperformed the 235B model with pass-at-one essentially doubling. The fine-tuned model demonstrated disciplined tool use: first calling get_table_names, then inspecting schema via get_table_info, running a query, hitting a column error, self-correcting, and getting the correct answer. Tool discipline, not reasoning, was the key behavior learned.

sections.title: Single-Table Training Transfer and Rubric-Based Evals
sections.summary: Single-table-only training yielded the greatest uplift and transferred to harder multi-table problems, improving FinQA reasoning from 13.9% to 26.6%. Crawford advocates rubric-based evals that break responses into granular questions to identify which specific behavior to fix before generating training data, while GRPO uses a single value for the RL cycle. A blog post and UC Berkeley partner post provide further details.
